headline: Models are now cheap to swap. Trust is not.
summary: The model is no longer your moat; the plumbing around it is your risk. In one week, GPT-6.2 Astra landed 0.3 points behind Fable 5.2 on one benchmark in a third of the time, Gemini 4 Neon use on Perplexity grew 15% a day, and Databricks found 75% of companies already run two or more model providers. Switching models has become a pricing call. Switching trust has not: OpenRouter dropped three inference providers after data incidents, and Guillermo Rauch argued that free inference sold as zero retention can move data to nation states at scale. The builders pulling ahead fence their agents in with verification gates, constrained tools and written decisions, since frontier models are rewarded per task, not for code you can maintain. Before your next model switch, ask where your tokens travel and who checks what comes back.

threads.title: Models became a line item
threads.line: Rankings and prices now move weekly. Keep two providers ready and choose on cost per solved task, not loyalty.

threads.title: The cheap pipe leaks
threads.line: Your weakest inference provider sets your data risk. Audit where prompts go before a discount decides for you.

threads.title: Less freedom, better code
threads.line: Reliable teams narrow what agents may choose and make them prove their work. Write the rules down.

threads.title: Walled apps, open harnesses
threads.line: Labs want you inside their app; builders want any model in one harness. Pick tools that let you leave.
